issues.failure_explanation: The paper initially permits an arbitrary source f in H^{-1}(Omega), but the element residual, its L2 norm, and the cellwise L1/L2 projection of s_h all treat f as a measurable function. For a general f in V*, these objects are undefined, so the hypotheses and conclusion of the residual majorant cannot be instantiated as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require the combined source s_h to belong to L2 elementwise (in particular, impose suitable function-space assumptions on f and the lower-order terms), or develop a different residual decomposition that handles general H^{-1} data.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised C1 construction and explicit flux reconstruction are unsupported for the paper's stated general source class f in V*; consequently, the full NK workflow is not established in that regime.
issues.title: Residual majorant requires a density for the abstract source
issues.why_classification: Adding an L2-type data hypothesis preserves the method but materially narrows the stated source class; retaining general V* data would require a nontrivial replacement residual construction.

issues.failure_explanation: For V=H^1_0(Omega) in dimensions two or three, no finite constant C_infinity can bound the L-infinity norm by the H1 energy norm for every v in V. The paper's own stated Sobolev ranges stop short of L-infinity in d=2 and at p=6 in d=3. issues.failure_explanation: Writing s_h^*=psi-partial_s c z_h gives G(v)=int s_h^*v-int A grad z_h·grad v. If div sigma_h^*=s_h^*, integration by parts gives G(v)=-int (sigma_h^*+A grad z_h)·grad v, so the mismatch is sigma_h^*+A grad z_h, not sigma_h^*-A grad z_h. Equivalently, the stated mismatch would require div sigma_h^*=-s_h^*.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, $\{\rho>0:\ p(\rho)\le 0\}$ is either empty or an interval of the form $[\rho_-,\rho_+]$ (possibly with $\rho_-=\rho_+$).

issues.failure_explanation: Intersecting the closed p-sublevel interval [a,b] with the open q-sublevel interval (0,rho_q) gives [a,b] when b<rho_q, not [a,b). Thus the upper endpoint may be admissible, and the admissible set may even be a singleton. The proof incorrectly changes every such intersection to a right-open interval and consequently asserts that admissibility always fails at its supremum.
